partially_covered.missing: Still limited to organization name, address, and identifier; no contact info, tax ID, or business registration attributes modeled. No properties for phone, email, or legal entity codes.

ValidationConstraint and ShaclConstraint classes exist, but there are still no explicit OWL restrictions or SHACL shapes for mandatory D96A fields. No enumerated list of required identifiers or enforced cardinality.

cq_coverage.details: Coverage remains largely unchanged: most CQs are fully addressed via structural modeling of invoices, organizations, items, pricing, and process assignment. CQ5 and CQ13 remain only partially addressed, as no new properties or constraints for business-relevant org attributes or D96A-required fields were added.

strengths: Class hierarchy and EDIFACT structure are rich and deep
Pivot classes and role reification are correctly modeled
Disjointness and equivalence axioms are present
weaknesses: No new general class axioms for mandatory D96A fields or role assignments
Organization modeling lacks further business attributes (e.g., contact, tax info)

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4: Future risk of missing domain/range if extended

reasoner_risks: Complex restrictions on pivot classes could slow Hermit/Pellet on large datasets, but no critical blocking constructs detected

improvement_tracking.notes: No substantive changes were made since the last review; all key improvement suggestions remain unaddressed. The ontology is stable and robust, but further enrichment is needed for full CQ and technical coverage.

summary: The ontology remains robust, well-structured, and OWL 2 compliant, with deep hierarchies and correct use of reification, restrictions, and annotations. However, none of the high-priority suggestions from the previous review were implemented: organization attributes and explicit validation logic for D96A compliance are still missing, and no new general class axioms or example data were added. Quality and coverage scores are unchanged. Further progress requires addressing these specific modeling gaps.
